alignments.note: Periphrastic hazeh hawayta rendered by the one verb sawest, with the subject pronoun rule 17 keeps with it (r30).
ad takes till. The pair is not fused as at 2.9, because here the ASV writes a second word for the di in particular (r30).
The written that answers to di.
Passive with its phrasal particle; the head stays on the lexical verb, since out alone names nothing (r44).
The indefinite a joins the noun that licenses it (r15).

Corrected. The one relative morpheme in the clause complex takes the ASV's one relative word, even though English writes it at the head of the second, coordinated predicate of the same relative (r25, r55); a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied reading does (r46, r47). Two competing readings: giving which to the waw, which rule 17 forbids for a recast clause's relative pronoun and which rule 14's open list does not reach, since which is not a connective; and reading which as the verb's own subject pronoun under rule 17, which would leave a written relative morpheme holding nothing. The word without carries only the negation and the preposition, so it does not absorb this di.
without carries the negation and the preposition in one English word (r30); headed on the negative.
Corrected. The ASV writes no connective for this waw: its clause is recast as the second predicate under the relative, and the single which belongs to di (r14, r17).
The verb keeps its own English; its subject is realized by the relative on di.
Object marker with no English of its own (r16).
Determined ending takes the written the (r15).

The material di takes that ... of together with the copula the construction supplies (r20, r41). The head could equally be of, which is what the same di takes at 2.32 and 2.33; I keep the relative, which is what the ASV's recasting of the phrase turns on.
brake in pieces, discontinuous around the object pronoun (r25); the head stays on the verb (r44).

review_notes: Corrected: the ASV's which is given to the relative di rather than to the waw. Rule 17 rules that a relative pronoun in a recast clause is not the waw's merely because it opens that clause, and rule 14's open list is a list of connectives, which a relative is not; di is the one relative morpheme standing in the clause complex, and without carries no relative sense that would absorb it.
The waw is then unrepresented, the ASV having written no connective for it (r14).
The rest of the accepted alignment stands; the head of the material di, which the ASV expands as that were of, is noted as a live tie with of, the reading taken at 2.32 and 2.33.
